title: Contains Duplicate
problem: Return true if any value appears at least twice in nums.
learner_message: Do the repeated values have to be next to each other?
teacher_message:
nums: [4, 7, 2, 4] → the last num=4 matches an earlier 4 → true

No. Repeated values can be anywhere in nums; they only need to be equal.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: Needs clarification that duplicates are defined by equal values, regardless of position.

model_assessment.rationale: The learner asks a question about adjacency but does not state the duplicate-property invariant.

title: Contains Duplicate
problem: Return true if any value appears at least twice in nums.
learner_message: So could I sort the list and just check neighboring numbers for a match?
teacher_message:
Visual:
nums: [4, 7, 2, 4] → sorted nums: [2, 4, 4, 7]
                                      num=num → true

Yes. Sorting makes equal values neighbors. Traverse nums and compare each neighboring pair: a match means a value appears at least twice; no match means return false.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: Proposes sorting and checking adjacent equality, but does not explicitly state the duplicate invariant.

model_assessment.rationale: The message is a question about a possible procedure, not a demonstrated semantic statement.

title: Contains Duplicate
problem: Return true if any value appears at least twice in nums.
learner_message: I understand: sorting puts duplicates next to each other, so matching neighbors means true.
teacher_message:
Visual:
nums: [4, 7, 2, 4] → sorted nums: [2, 4, 4, 7]
                                      num = num → true

Exactly. After sorting, equal neighboring values identify a duplicate. If every neighboring pair differs, return false.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: Connects equal neighboring values after sorting to the duplicate condition.

model_assessment.evidence_quote: sorting puts duplicates next to each other, so matching neighbors means true
model_assessment.rationale: The learner states that equal values indicate a duplicate after sorting.

title: Contains Duplicate
problem: Return true if any value appears at least twice in nums.
learner_message: If the list has only one number, do I return false?
teacher_message:
Visual:
nums: [8] → box: {} → num=8 is not in box → box: {8} → false

Yes. With only one number, no duplicate pair can exist, so return false.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: Checks a one-element boundary case without defining tracked state or a duplicate-detection invariant.

model_assessment.rationale: The message asks about the return value for a single-element list but does not demonstrate the seen-values state or invariant.

title: Contains Duplicate
problem: Return true if any value appears at least twice in nums.
learner_message: Wait, is the box another way to solve it instead of sorting?
teacher_message:
Visual:
nums: [4, 7, 2, 4] → box: {} → num=4 → box: {4} → num=7 → box: {4, 7} → num=2 → box: {2, 4, 7} → num=4 is already in box → true

Yes. box is another approach instead of sorting. It stores the distinct values processed earlier in nums: add num when it is not in box; return true when num is already in box. If nums finishes without a match, return false.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: Asks whether the seen-value set is an alternative to sorting, without defining its state or operation.

model_assessment.rationale: The learner asks a comparison question but does not demonstrate the seen-set invariant or membership-and-insert behavior.

title: Contains Duplicate
problem: Return true if any value appears at least twice in nums.
learner_message: Okay, the box stores numbers I’ve seen, so I return true when one appears again.
teacher_message:
Visual:
nums: [4, 7, 2, 4] → box: {} → num=4 → box: {4} → num=7 → box: {4, 7} → num=2 → box: {2, 4, 7} → num=4 is already in box → true

Correct. Traverse nums in order; before each num, box contains exactly the distinct earlier values. Add num if absent, return true if it is already present, and return false if nums finishes without a match.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: Describes tracking seen values and detecting a repeat.

model_assessment.evidence_quote: the box stores numbers I’ve seen, so I return true when one appears again.
model_assessment.rationale: The message identifies the tracked prior values and the condition that indicates a duplicate.

title: Contains Duplicate
problem: Return true if any value appears at least twice in nums.
learner_message: Do I check whether the number is already in the box before adding it?
teacher_message:
Visual:
num=4, box={} → 4 is not in box → add 4 → box={4}
num=4, box={4} → 4 is in box → return true

Yes. Check whether num is in box first. If it is not, add num; if it is already there, a duplicate has been detected.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: Asks whether membership is checked before insertion.

model_assessment.rationale: This is a question about operation order, not a demonstrated explanation of the concept.

title: Contains Duplicate
problem: Return true if any value appears at least twice in nums.
learner_message: I might be mixing it up—do I add the number first and then check for a duplicate?
teacher_message:
Visual:
num=4, box={} → 4 is not in box → add 4 → box={4}
num=4, box={4} → 4 is in box → return true

Check whether num is in box first. If it is not, add num to box; if it is already there, return true.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: Confuses whether to check membership before inserting a value.

model_assessment.rationale: The learner asks about reversing the operation order and does not demonstrate the concept.

title: Contains Duplicate
problem: Return true if any value appears at least twice in nums.
learner_message: Got it: I check first, add only new numbers, and return true if it’s already there.
teacher_message:
Visual:
num=4, box={} → 4 is not in box → add 4 → box={4}
num=4, box={4} → 4 is in box → return true

Exactly: check whether num is in box first. If absent, add num; if already present, return true. If processing finishes without a match, return false.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: Checks membership before inserting unseen values.

model_assessment.evidence_quote: Got it: I check first, add only new numbers, and return true if it’s already there.
model_assessment.rationale: The learner explicitly states checking first, adding only new numbers, and detecting duplicates when a value is already present.

title: Contains Duplicate
problem: Return true if any value appears at least twice in nums.
learner_message: If I finish the list without finding a repeat, do I return false?
teacher_message:
Visual:
nums: [4, 7, 2] → check each num → add if absent → nums finished → false

Yes. Return false only after nums is fully processed without finding a repeat. Return true immediately when num is already in box.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: Asks whether to return false after nums is exhausted without a repeat.

model_assessment.rationale: The learner asks a confirmation question but does not independently demonstrate the terminal-result rule.

title: Contains Duplicate
problem: Return true if any value appears at least twice in nums.
learner_message: So if the current number is new, I shouldn’t return false yet—I have to keep checking?
teacher_message:
Visual:
nums: [4, 7, 2] → num=4, box={} → add 4 → continue
nums finished with no match → return false

nums: [4, 7, 2, 4] → final num=4, box={2, 4, 7} → already in box → return true

Yes. If num is new, add it to box and keep checking the rest of nums. Return false only after nums is fully processed without finding a duplicate.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: Learner is asking whether false is deferred until nums is exhausted.

model_assessment.rationale: The message is a question seeking confirmation and does not itself demonstrate the concept.

title: Contains Duplicate
problem: Return true if any value appears at least twice in nums.
learner_message: Okay, I’ll add new values and keep going, then return false only after the whole list has no duplicates.
teacher_message:
Visual:
nums: [4, 7, 2, 4] → box={} → num=4: not in box → add 4 → continue
num=4 with box={2, 4, 7} → already in box → return true
nums: [4, 7, 2] → nums finished without a match → return false

Check num in box before adding. Add num only when absent and continue; return true immediately when num is already in box. Return false only after nums is fully processed without a duplicate.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: Recognizes that new values require continued processing and false is returned only after nums is exhausted without duplicates.

model_assessment.evidence_quote: Okay, I’ll add new values and keep going, then return false only after the whole list has no duplicates.
model_assessment.rationale: The message states the correct continuation rule and terminal false condition.
